note: REJECTED on user steer: auto-restamping the 'safe' quadrant silently accepts code that was never re-checked against its binding rule. A hash refresh is not a verification — it only records that the code is now different. No anchor may advance without an explicit audit verdict. Superseded by the re-audit design (P-0061): drift triggers a mandatory, automatic audit of the NEW code against the prevailing rules; only a pass re-stamps.
sum: proposal automate anchor re-stamping: use RHash to classify drift direction, auto-heal the safe quadrant, gate done on clean anchors — Empirical finding from this development cycle: the orchestrator had to hand-run `rule op=edit id=X applies=[node]` roughly ten times, always after the same pattern — a LEGITIMATE code change to an anchored function, then `d changed`, then TestCheckOnOwnRepo fai
body: Empirical finding from this development cycle: the orchestrator had to hand-run `rule op=edit id=X applies=[node]` roughly ten times, always after the same pattern — a LEGITIMATE code change to an anchored function, then `d changed`, then TestCheckOnOwnRepo fails, then a manual re-stamp. That is pure toil the server can do itself. Root cause: internal/drift.Anchor stores BOTH CHash (normalized code span) and RHash (normalized rule sentence), but drift.Classify only ever compares CHash — so every kind of divergence collapses into one 'changed' class that a human must resolve. Design: (1) DIRECTION-AWARE CLASSIFICATION — compare both hashes and yield a 2x2: code-same+rule-same = OK; code-changed+rule-same = ImplementationEvolved (the contract still says what it said; the implementation moved); code-same+rule-changed = ContractTightened (spec now promises something the code was never re-checked against — the DANGEROUS direction, today completely invisible); both-changed = Diverged. (2) AUTO-HEAL THE SAFE QUADRANT — for ImplementationEvolved, check re-stamps CHash automatically (exactly like the existing silent refresh for position-only 'moved'), emits one dense record `d restamped <rule> <node>` and appends a journal event so it stays auditable and git-reversible. This alone removes the ten manual calls. (3) SURFACE THE DANGEROUS ONE — ContractTightened must NOT auto-heal; it drafts a backprop proposal (or at minimum a loud finding), because a contract that changed without its code being revalidated is a silent spec/code lie. (4) CLOSE THE LOOP IN THE LIFECYCLE — `move to=done` verifies the anchors bound to the item's targets and refuses (or auto-heals per rule 2) while they drift, so 'done' cannot be reached with stale anchors; the existing rounds/blocked machinery already handles gate failures. Honest tradeoff to record: auto-restamping ImplementationEvolved assumes 'rule text unchanged = intent unchanged' and never re-validates the contract against the new implementation. Mitigations: every auto-restamp is journaled (auditable), it is reversible in git, and the risky direction stays manual. Exit criterion (explicit): drift.Classify returns the four direction-aware classes with unit tests per quadrant (incl. RHash-only change); check auto-restamps ImplementationEvolved and journals it; ContractTightened produces a finding/backprop and never auto-heals; a lifecycle test proves move-to-done is gated on the item's anchors; running check on this repo after a deliberate anchored-function edit yields `d restamped` and NO manual rule call; go test ./... -race green; docs/lifecycle.md + docs/tools.md document the four classes. Rollback: revert; anchors.tsv format is unchanged (both hashes already exist). Scope: internal/drift/drift.go + drift_test.go, internal/mcpserver/tools.go (check), internal/lifecycle/lifecycle.go (done gate), docs.

body: IMPLEMENTER IN A DEDICATED WORKTREE (pre-created at .claude/worktrees/impl-m, based on HEAD); NO lifecycle moves (orchestrator owns them); only lease claim, code+tests, lease release, report. Scope (disjoint): internal/migrate/ (NEW package: migrate.go + migrate_test.go), cmd/spectackle/main.go, cmd/spectackle/main_test.go. A sibling implementer owns README.md and docs/ RIGHT NOW — do NOT touch any doc file. Do NOT touch internal/mcpserver, internal/workspace, internal/lifecycle, internal/item. Goal: the ONLY sanctioned way to rewrite legacy decision ids is a server-side operation; hand-editing .spectackle is forbidden by the architecture. Build `spectackle migrate-adr [-root DIR] [-apply]`. Behavior: (1) Walk every .spectackle context bundle in the workspace (use the same discovery the rest of the code uses — workspace.Detect for the root, then workspace.Root.ContextDirs() for the context list; read work.md and journal.ndjson per context via their existing paths, e.g. Root.WorkPath(ctx) and the journal file next to it). (2) Find every occurrence of a legacy item id matching the exact pattern `D-<4 digits>` (regexp `\bD-\d{4}\b`) in those files — both in item headings/bodies of work.md and in journal.ndjson lines (the journal is NDJSON: rewrite the id inside the JSON values, do NOT reformat the JSON — a plain textual replacement of the id token is correct and keeps every other byte identical). (3) The replacement is the same number with the ADR prefix: ADR-0010 -> ADR-0010. (4) COLLISION GUARD: before writing anything, if any target id (ADR-<same digits>) already exists anywhere in the workspace, abort with a clear error naming the collision and change nothing. (5) DRY RUN BY DEFAULT: without -apply, print one dense line per planned rewrite — `m <file> ADR-0010 -> ADR-0010 x<count>` — plus a trailing `ok <n> ids in <m> files (dry-run; pass -apply to write)`, and exit 0 without modifying anything. With -apply, perform the rewrites and print `ok migrated <n> ids in <m> files`. (6) IDEMPOTENT: a second run finds nothing and prints `ok nothing to migrate`. Wire the subcommand into cmd/spectackle/main.go's run() dispatch exactly like the existing lint/reindex subcommands (they use rootFlag-style flag parsing and return an int exit code) and add it to the usage() text. Tests: internal/migrate/migrate_test.go over a fixture workspace built in a t.TempDir() containing (a) a root .spectackle/work.md with a live `## ADR-0010 some decision` item block, (b) a root .spectackle/journal.ndjson with lines referencing ADR-0010 and ADR-0011, (c) a nested context bundle with no D ids at all — assert: dry-run reports the right files/counts and changes no bytes; apply rewrites exactly the ids and leaves every other byte identical (compare the full file contents against the expected string); a second apply reports nothing to migrate; and a fixture where ADR-0010 already exists causes an error with no writes. Add one cmd-level test in main_test.go asserting run([]string{"migrate-adr", tmpdir}) returns 0 in dry-run. Verify: go vet ./internal/migrate/ ./cmd/spectackle/ && go test ./internal/migrate/ ./cmd/spectackle/ -race && go test ./... -race && make build && ./bin/spectackle lint . (must stay 15/61/0). IMPORTANT: do NOT run migrate-adr -apply against the real repo — the orchestrator does that deliberately after review. Report the dry-run output shape and the test list. Rollback: delete internal/migrate, revert main.go.
